NATIONAL FOREWORD This Indian Standard which is identical with 1S0 13734 : 1998 `Natural gas -- Organic sulfur compounds used as odorants -- Requirements and test methods' issued by the International Organization for Standardization ( ISO ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on the recommendation of the Natural Gas Sectional Committee and approval of the Petroleum, Coal and Related Products Division Council. The text of ISO Standard has been approved as suitable for publication as Indian Standard without deviations. Certain conventions are, however, not identical to those used in Indian Standards. 4 4.1

Requirements Composition

The mass content of organic sulfur compounds in the undiluted odorant when determined in accordance with 6.3 shall be equal to or higher than 95 Yo. At least 80 ?fo of the mass content of these sulfur compounds shall consist of sulfides (thioethers) or secondary or tertiary mercaptans (thiols). The composition of the odorant, and where applicable the dilution range, shall be declared by the producer or distributor. .{ NOTE -- Primary mercaptans -- especially methyl and ethyl mercaptan -- are more easily oxidized than secondaty or tertiary mercaptans by traces of oxygen in the gas and by iron oxide, e.g. in the form of pipe dust. It is therefore
recommended that the content of primaty mercaptans in odorants be minimized.

Cloud point in accordance with 6.4, shall be below -30 "C.

4.6

Volubility

in water (optional requirement)

When the odorant is added to water in the way specified in 6.8, less than 2 % by volume of the odorant shall be soluble. This optional requirement is valid for wet distribution systems.

IS 15319:2003 ISO 13734:1998 5 Handling and transport by a safety data sheet conforming to the requirements

When delivered, odorants shall be accompanied of the country of use. 6 6.1 Tests Test sample

For type approval and control tests, the producer or supplier shall deliver at least 0,5 I of a representative sample of the liquid odorant to a qualified test laboratory, acceptable to both producer and purchaser.

6.2

Test documentation shall be provided by the producer or supplier: of the country of use;

The following documentation a) b)

a safety data sheet conforming to the requirements complete details of the composition of the odorant.

6.3

Determination

of composition

The composition of the odorant shall be determined by gas-chromatographic analysis on a 50 m methyl silicone capillary column (internal diameter 0,2 mm) with a carrier gas (Hz or He) at a flow rate of 1,8 ml/min and a split ratio of 1:30. The initial temperature shall be 35 `C; after 10 rein, the temperature shall be raised at a rate of 7 OC/min to 250 `C and kept at this temperature. For the detection of sulfur and non-sulfur compounds (diluents or impurities), a non-sulfur-specific detector -- e.g. a flame ionization detector (FID) or a thermal-conductivity detector (TCD) -- shall be used, The response functions of the various sulfur compounds shall be determined with calibration mixtures prepared from pure components. The concentrations of impurities which cannot be identified shall be calculated on the basis of the response factor for n-hexane. The retention times of the relevant sulfur compounds in relation to the retention time of tetrahydrothiophene (THT), which is about 15 rein, are given in table 1, which also lists the boiling points. Any gas-chromatographic method giving equivalent, or better, component separation be used. In cases of dispute, the above-mentioned method shall be used. A sulfur-specific components. detector may additionally be used to differentiate between and detection may

sulfur

and non-sulfur

6.4

Determination

of cloud point

The cloud point shall be determined in accordance with ISO 3015 except that, contrary to the method specified in that standard, cloud formation by water shall be taken into accounfi therefore the sample shall be neither filtered nor dried. The test jar in its jacket is directly immersed in bath No. 4 specified in table 2 of ISO 3015:1992 having the temperature range �52 "C to -49 "C. When the temperature of the

and inspected

for cloudiness.

6.7

Visual examination

for solids or suspended

matter

Take a sample of about 20 ml of the odorant in a normal test tube of about 15 mm internal diameter and inspect it after shaking and again after a settling time of 15 rein, against a light source, for insoluble material.

6.8

Determination

of volubility

in water

Add 5 ml of the odorant to 50 ml of a 10% solution of sodium chloride in water in a graduated glass cylinder (see figure 1) with a ground-in plug. Measure the volume of the odorant in the graduated part of the cylinder with the cylinder in the upright position ( ~).

Marking in accordance with applicable safety and transport

Odorant containers shall be clearly marked regulations. The markings will normally include: a) b) c)
